Subject: Adaptive degradation SLA request — AtlasVision preview ramp

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for agreeing to run the AtlasVision preview with us. Your engineering team’s telemetry looked great during the POC, and we’re excited to support Holloway’s visual search experiment. Before we flip the canary traffic over, we need to formalize a short-lived SLA exemption for the preview model (AtlasVision v0.9).

Ask in plain terms: can Holloway accept a temporary, documented deviation from our standard 99.95% 99th-percentile latency guarantee for the first 30 days of preview? The deviation we recommend is an adaptive-degradation policy that does three things when tail latency rises: 1) route low-priority requests to a cheaper quantized variant, 2) enable prefix-KV caching for repeated contexts, and 3) raise the acceptable 99th-percentile latency floor from 200ms to 650ms for a rolling 24-hour window, with automatic rollback if errors exceed 0.5%.

I’ve attached two artifacts: a CSV with the preview metrics we observed during the POC and a short proposal that maps the policy to Redwood’s monitoring/rollback hooks. If this sounds acceptable, we’ll draft a one-page exception letter for your procurement team and open a short ticket in HubSpot for tracking (HS-987452).

Next steps I propose:
- Olivia: confirm the 30-day window and the proposed latency floor (650ms)
- Holloway legal/procurement: sign the one-page exception (we’ll produce)
- Engineering: agree on telemetry signals for automatic rollback (we’ll share thresholds)

We want to preserve availability while avoiding surprise throttles during the initial ramp. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to review the policy.

Best,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — appreciated. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side before we sign anything:

1) Can you confirm whether routed "low-priority" requests will preserve result fidelity for our ranking pipeline? We have a handful of batch re-ranks that are latency-sensitive for user-facings.
2) If the 99th jumps repeatedly above 650ms during the 30 days, what mitigation will Redwood take to protect customer-facing queries?
3) We’ll need a simple escalation path with an on-call contact for the preview window.

We’re generally okay with a temporary relaxation if we can keep clear guardrails around fidelity and an on-call. We plan to start canarying 10% of production traffic next Monday and ramp to 50% over two weeks.

—Olivia

Marcus / Dev —

Draft language we should use for the one-page exception (internal draft):

- Duration: 30 calendar days from first production canary traffic (documented start)
- SLO deviation: 99th percentile latency allowance increased to 650ms for a rolling 24-hour window
- Hard error cap: if error rate (5xx + model failures) for customer routes exceeds 0.5% in a 1-hour window, Redwood will execute automatic rollback to the last stable model variant and notify Holloway immediately
- Fidelity protection: Redwood will not apply lossy-quantized variants to requests flagged as CUSTOMER_RANKING unless explicitly white-listed by Holloway
- Observability: 1-minute reporting cadence to the shared dashboard and webhook alerts for thresholds

I’ll plug this into our standard exception template and send it to Marcus to forward. Dev: need your note on expected KV-cache hit improvements and whether the 650ms floor is realistic for the anticipated 50% traffic ramp.

-Laura

Quick technical note for the thread and for Holloway:

- With prefix-KV caching enabled for repeated contexts, we saw a 14–22% median latency improvement in the POC and a 35% reduction in tokenized work on repeated image queries (see attached csv).
- The quantized fallback variant preserves ranking order for >95% of queries in our offline evals; we only block quantization for CUSTOMER_RANKING by default.
- 650ms 99th is conservative for the initial ramp; under 50% traffic it should be reachable provided cache hit-rate stays above ~40%. If hit-rate falls below 20% for a sustained 3-hour window, we recommend automatic rollback.

I’ll add a line to the one-page exception for the automatic rollback trigger and the on-call escalation (pager: eng-oncall@redwood.ai).

-Dev
Dev Patel | Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the quick questions. Short answers inline, and then a proposal below.

> 1) Fidelity for routing to low-priority variants?
We will preserve ranking fidelity for any request you mark as CUSTOMER_RANKING by route header. Quantized fallback will never apply to those by default.

> 2) If 99th jumps repeatedly above 650ms?
We’ve defined an automatic rollback condition: if error rate rises above 0.5% in an hour OR if cache hit-rate <20% for 3 continuous hours, Redwood will rollback to the last stable model (no quantized fallback) and notify your team immediately.

> 3) On-call contact?
Pager: eng-oncall@redwood.ai; Primary contact for this preview: Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwood.ai). We’ll also create a dedicated Slack channel for faster coordination.

Proposal (actionable):
- Start canary 10% on 2027-06-07, ramp to 50% by 2027-06-21
- 30-day exception from first canary production day (expected start 2027-06-07)
- Redwood to produce one-page exception and push to Holloway legal by EOD Thu 2027-06-03
- Weekly check-ins during ramp (Mon 09:00 PT) and immediate notifications on rollback criteria

If you approve the above, I’ll attach the final exception and route it to your procurement.

Thanks —
Marcus

We’ll sign as soon as we receive the one-pager. Looking forward to the 10% canary next week.

—Olivia
